title: SB 1383 support for jurisdictions
summary: Plan organics education, food recovery inspections, business support, and reporting with a local program partner.
offerings: Food recovery inspections and capacity planning
nextStep: Discuss your jurisdiction, service scope, and contract needs with the Environmental Solutions team.
statusNote: Services are arranged with jurisdictions. Coverage and scope depend on the contract.

title: Business organics and food recovery help
summary: Get guidance on organics recycling and edible food recovery. Access bilingual resources and help with local SB 1383 procedures.
nextStep: Contact the SB 1383 team to confirm service coverage for your business and city.
statusNote: Solana Center works under city contracts. Confirm coverage; using these resources does not establish compliance.

title: Food donation setup resources
summary: Use practical resources to set up a food donation program and coordinate surplus food recovery.
nextStep: Read the guides, then confirm arrangements with a food recovery organization and your city.
statusNote: Resources support planning. This listing does not offer food collection or a public food drop-off.

title: Food recovery inspection training
summary: Learn edible food recovery requirements and inspection methods through scheduled live training and on-demand fundamentals.
nextStep: Compare the course formats and check the next live session or interest list.
statusNote: Live dates vary. Fundamentals alone are not the full inspection training; the full live course spans three days.

title: Home composting and Master Composter courses
summary: Learn backyard composting, worm composting, and bokashi. Use practical guides or follow a scheduled course.
nextStep: Read the guides and check the event calendar for the next course.
statusNote: Guides are available now. Course dates vary; this is education, not a food scrap drop-off service.

title: Manure composting consultation
summary: Get help with manure management, compost system selection, and site-specific compost problems.
nextStep: Contact the education team to confirm eligibility and book a call.
statusNote: Free consultations are for eligible residents of unincorporated San Diego County. Confirm eligibility before booking.

title: Healthy Soils grant technical assistance
summary: Get technical help to carry out awarded Healthy Soils practices, document work, and report results.
nextStep: Ask about assistance for your award, or join the interest list for a future grant cycle.
statusNote: The grant application window is closed. The page offers free technical assistance to awardees; it does not promise new funding.

title: School lessons and lunch waste sorting
summary: Bring environmental lessons and practical waste sorting support to schools. Topics include compost, watersheds, and textiles.
nextStep: School staff can submit the program interest form to confirm scope, dates, and cost.
statusNote: Many offerings are free for unincorporated County schools in 2026–27. Other school costs depend on grant availability.

title: Lunch & Learn for your team
summary: Bring practical sustainability lessons to your team in person or online.
nextStep: Choose a topic and request a quote for your group.
statusNote: Presentations are arranged for groups. Confirm the format, date, and price.

title: Waste reduction support for events
summary: Plan waste stations, guide event visitors, and assess the waste left after your event.
nextStep: Share your event size, site, and date to discuss services and cost.
statusNote: Service levels and fees vary. Waste diversion results depend on the event and available collection services.

title: Plastic waste prevention support
summary: Reduce disposable plastic through education, business consultations, reuse, and better waste systems.
nextStep: Describe your waste stream and goals through the program contact form.
statusNote: Services are arranged by request. This listing does not represent producer responsibility registration or certification.

title: Textile reuse and repair education
summary: Help your community extend the life of clothing through swaps, mending, upcycling, and textile waste education.
nextStep: Request a group program or check the current textile event schedule.
statusNote: Education and group programs are offered by request. The next listed expo is May 8, 2027; this is not a general textile drop-off.

title: Rainwater and watershed learning
summary: Learn how to collect rainwater, reduce polluted runoff, and care for water-wise gardens and landscapes.
nextStep: Read the water resources and check current workshops or contact staff for help.
statusNote: Education resources remain available. The Sustainability Shop is closed; check current events for any special distributions.

title: Tool Lending Library
summary: Rent household and garden tools for home, school, and community garden projects in San Diego County.
nextStep: Create a rental account, review the terms and fees, and reserve online.
statusNote: Online reservation required. Friday pickup/return, noon–3 pm, at St. Andrew's Church parking lot, 890 Balour Dr, Encinitas. Rental fees apply.

title: Green Convene reusable dishware
summary: Rent reusable plates, bowls, drinkware, and utensils for local gatherings.
nextStep: Check stock and rental terms, then reserve the item types and quantities you need online.
statusNote: Online reservation required. Friday pickup/return, noon–3 pm, at St. Andrew's Church parking lot, 890 Balour Dr, Encinitas. Rental and other fees apply.

title: Plastic Beach subscriber drop-off
summary: Plastic Beach subscribers can use Solana Center’s hosted drop-off for selected plastic bags and film.
nextStep: Check subscription terms, accepted materials, and current drop-off hours before you visit.
sourceTitle: Plastic Recycling Program – Thanks to Plastic Beach!
statusNote: Subscribers only, at 137 N. El Camino Real, Encinitas. Materials must be clean, dry, and empty; many wrappers are excluded. Confirm hours.

sources.title: Plastic Recycling Program – Thanks to Plastic Beach!
